A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MRD research. All 16 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v3, including supplementary text, equations, tables, plots and qualitative examples, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MRD benchmark results, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments and qualitative retrieval examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original MRD evaluations and adds failure-mode measurements, inference-efficiency results, and resolution-scale and detection-threshold ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use two-resolution VisRAG scores, geometric-mean semantic fusion, LLM-extracted detection targets, sliding-window LLMDet, confidence averaging, linear map fusion and RAP search. Additional resolution combinations are ablation variants; the changed search-step limit is an experimental setting rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate V* Bench and HR-Bench 4K/8K with the same single-object and multi-object task coverage. The new diagnostics, efficiency measurements and sensitivity studies use these retained benchmarks without establishing a new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: v1 Appendix B.5 and Table 3 evaluate DC2 alongside RAP and Zoom Eye; this comparison disappears from v3, with no DC2 results retained elsewhere. The comparator membership in main Table 1 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A revises the stated default maximum search budget from 200 to 50 steps. v3 also introduces manual, potentially overlapping failure-category coding, stage-wise runtime and peak-memory measurements, and additional resolution-scale and detection-threshold sweeps. These substantially extend the evaluation protocol; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative fragmentation/background-error analysis in Section 3.2 and Table 2, resolution-combination ablations in Appendix B.2/Table 4, and detection-threshold sensitivity in Appendix B.6/Figure 10. Existing crop-resolution, search-budget, fusion-weight and window-size studies remain. Figure 2 replaces the motivating case study, while Figure 5 reduces four module examples to two.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new error percentages and average runtimes are descriptive results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds failure-rate, runtime/memory, resolution-combination and threshold results, while removing the DC2 results. Table 1 changes LLaVA-ov MRD spatial/overall accuracy from 82.9/88.0 to 85.6/88.9, and LLaVA-v1.5 MRD HR-Bench 4K/8K overall scores from 59.7/54.9 to 59.9/54.8. Table 2 changes full-MRD overall accuracy from 89.3 to 88.9. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains given the changed search budget.

T1.justification: The mathematical operations defining semantic similarity, geometric-mean fusion, detection filtering, confidence aggregation and linear fusion remain equivalent. Equation edits simplify notation, correct coordinate indexing and remove a redundant coordinate identity; neither version contains added theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 removes v1's explicit claim to be the first work systematically using open-vocabulary detection to enhance HR image understanding, and emphasizes unified modeling of local semantic integrity and global spatial grounding. The central training-free MRD contribution and strong single-object/multi-object performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive limitations section identifying missed small, occluded or crowded objects, detector saliency bias, and dependence on fixed windows and hand-designed fusion settings. It also interprets fragmentation/background errors as dominant bottlenecks, discusses backbone-dependent benefits of extra resolutions, and explains the runtime-versus-memory tradeoff. These extend v1's narrower qualitative mechanism and tuning discussions.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies a detection confidence threshold of 0.3 and supplies a repository address with a promise of future code availability. It no longer explicitly states v1's answering confidence threshold of 0.6; these are distinct thresholds, not evidence of a 0.6-to-0.3 setting change. Crop sizes, window/stride pairs, resolution ratio and fusion weight remain documented.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially expanded and reorganized around HR architectures, reasoning-guided search, attention-guided localization and reinforcement learning. Newly discussed works include TextCoT, Zoom-Refine, HiDE, FOCUS and Pixel Reasoner, alongside broader MLLM application literature. Positioning also shifts away from the explicit first-detector-use claim.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, results discussion and supplementary prose. It merges the separate module-effect discussions, introduces clearer experimental subsections, reorganizes the appendix, and changes the author/affiliation block. This exceeds localized editing despite the stable method.

P2.justification: v3 replaces Figure 2, redraws Figure 3 with an overall-performance panel, revises the framework diagram, and condenses Figure 5. Table 2 gains error-rate columns; new efficiency and resolution tables and a threshold plot are added, while v1's supplementary comparison table is removed. Retained appendix plots and qualitative figures are relabeled and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 provides better diagnostic support and clearer applicability boundaries through targeted ablations, efficiency measurements and explicit limitations. It also reconciles the full-MRD overall accuracy between Tables 1 and 2 at 88.9. The net improvement is limited by lost DC2 coverage and new reporting inconsistencies: Section 3.2 reverses Table 2's BG/FRAG labels, and Table 3 labels the 63.4-to-53.4-second reduction as 26.2% rather than approximately 15.8%.
